items.title: No trial in a district with poor dental access
items.whyItMatters: The retrieved trial's practices had better dental access than average (claim c1); the effect may differ where the triage line is the only route.
items.opportunity: Test the pathway in the network with the triage line as a core component.

items.title: Safety of reduced prescribing where dental care is scarce
items.whyItMatters: Admissions for spreading infection are rare (claim c2) but could rise if antibiotics are withheld without treatment.
items.opportunity: Pre-specify emergency attendance and admission for dental infection as balancing measures with a safety review.

items.title: Two sources undated and unrated
items.whyItMatters: The triage service report and the guidance leaflet give no year and too little detail to rate.
items.opportunity: Keep them unrated; use them only for design ideas, not effect sizes.

items.title: Deprivation and dental access
items.whyItMatters: People without a dentist are concentrated in deprived neighbourhoods and consult GPs more.
items.opportunity: Stratify allocation by practice deprivation and report outcomes by deprivation fifth.

reevaluation: The gaps support a cluster randomised trial in the network with a safety balancing measure and stratification by deprivation.
summary: Four gaps: applicability, safety, undated sources and deprivation.
